recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It fixes the refactor carry-forward gap without narrowing the required binding or adding redundant narrative outside the authoritative StructureDefinition source.
issue_request: FHIR-32194 asked to narrow the value set for Measure.basis because some all-types codes are not useful as population basis values. It was Published with a Not Persuasive with Modification resolution: keep the all-FHIR-types binding for Measure.basis and Measure.group.basis, but document that population criteria can result in abstract types and that authoring environments may apply content-driven constraints.
initial_application: Commit 14927613a0a69db2add0762b1174e242356a91d4 applied FHIR-32194 by adding the abstract-type and authoring-environment clarification to the then-current root Measure.basis requirements text.
additional_context: FHIR-32079 records the same no-narrowing decision for the CQF Measures populationBasis extension. FHIR-32069 changed the terminology surface from ValueSet/all-types to ValueSet/fhir-types. Later R6 Measure refactors, especially FHIR-49922 and FHIR-50664, moved calculation definition to group-level elements and removed root Measure.basis, leaving Measure.group.basis as the active source location. FHIR-50500 added Measure.group.basisRequirement and includes an example where Resource is used as the broad basis while DataRequirements carry more specific counted-case detail.
reconciliation: Updated source/measure/structuredefinition-Measure.xml so Measure.group.basis requirements now state that the all-FHIR-types binding can include abstract types such as Resource and DomainResource, and that authoring environments may constrain this further based on content needs.
source_changes: source/measure/structuredefinition-Measure.xml: clarified Measure.group.basis requirements to preserve the FHIR-32194 abstract-type and authoring-environment guidance on the current group-level element.
